## 2. Decisions already made by the owner
- Plan tiers: Free and Katara get no studios; **Saka gets Sound Studio + Sound Library; the top plan (`all`, includes Yakko) gets everything** including Texture Studio + Texture Library. Tiers are cumulative.
- **Automatic asset generation follows the user's plan and access** (same gate whether Cyrus, the studio or a library creates the asset).
- **Mod Packs are not gated by plan. Importing your own mod to work on it is not gated by plan.**
- Asset libraries and studios are top priorities; the owner's 514-file sound library is the Sound Library seed.
- Everything in scope, ambitious timeline; launch is months away. Research ran as limited Sonnet agents; no parallel agent sprawl.
- Parked by the owner ("later"): Mojang EULA / marketplace question, other-platform AI policies (Modrinth etc.), licence review of dependencies. Not worked in this plan.

**Defaults I set (change any of them):**
- Gate semantics: gates apply to **creating or editing** assets. Installing, keeping, rebuilding unchanged and exporting existing project assets is never gated. The router downgrades (no custom asset) instead of erroring, and gating fails closed when token state is unknown.
- Banshee on 1.21.x = custom skin + full sound set on a vanilla-model mob; **animated custom-model creatures are 26.x first** (BetterModel v3 needs Java 25).
- Generated mods stay on `plugin.yml` (Paper's `paper-plugin.yml` is still experimental).
- Gameplay Designers, full creature pipeline and worldgen come after the foundation, assets and composition (they are mini-languages each).

## 2b. Built to stand alone later (owner decision, 2026-10-10)
Cyrus stays a part of Nxeon for at least the next few months (to build a solid foundation and gather months of real Nxeon-customer usage data), then may become its own product. So:
- **Nothing breaks and nothing changes for customers:** same sign-in, same accounts, same wallet, same billing. No separate Cyrus login now.
- **Design for the split from day one (cheap now, expensive later):** Cyrus code reaches Nxeon only through a small **host seam** (sign-in/user, plan and billing, server access for install, storage, notifications). New code must not add new direct imports of Nxeon internals; where one is unavoidable it goes behind a named adapter. Cyrus tables stay Cyrus-prefixed with opaque ids for users/servers (no new foreign keys into Nxeon tables). The build service already stands alone; the engine core, asset pipelines, Test Flight and pack hosting already live under `lib/cyrus/` and stay game- and host-agnostic.
- **Later, when separating:** Nxeon implements the host side as an API (list servers, push plugin/pack/config, restart); a standalone Cyrus gets its own sign-in, wallet and billing, own database, and a standalone export (jar and pack download). The Kodely-to-Nxeon partner API is the existing pattern.
- **Not now:** no code that exists only to prepare the split beyond the seam rule and a coupling map.

### 4.3 Capability router + task spec (M)
After the prompt check: classify what the request needs (plugin / plugin + resource pack / datapack / future client mod), disclose limits, show an editable plan and acceptance criteria before tokens are spent. One schema: this is the Master Plan's `CyrusTaskSpec`, the Roadmap's Mod Specification and the asset manifest. Tier gate is applied here and again inside the build service request.

### 4.4 Generators, build and reproducibility (M)
### 4.11 Data packs (M)
Typed spec -> per-version emitters (the AI never hand-writes JSON); schema source vanilla-mcdoc (MIT); static validation then boot a real headless Paper and test over RCON. MVP: recipes, loot, advancements, tags, functions, enchantments. Worldgen (biomes, structures, dimensions) later; `/reload` does not reload worldgen, so those changes need a restart.

## 5. Roadmap (ordered by dependency)
### R2 Composition, data packs, import (about 7 days)
| Day | Deliver | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| 10-11 | Static conflict engine on the inventory; severity report; reserved-namespace behaviour; mutation corpus (take a good mod, collide IDs) | Seeded conflicts caught with the right class and severity |
| 12 | Mod Pack Builder: manifest, merge (Weld/Beet evaluation), combined boot + differential boots, install/rollback as one unit | Two conflicting mods are caught, resolved or blocked; pack installs and rolls back as a unit |
| 13-14 | Datapack MVP: typed emitters per version, mcdoc validation, boot + RCON check | Valid datapack loads on every listed version |
| 15-16 | Import (source-only): ingestion limits, allowlist, attestation, strict vs attested scan, revision 0, change planner | An uploaded simple plugin source is edited by prompt, rebuilt, scanned, tested, installed; history kept |
| 16 | Public pass-rate page + evidence badges (boot-tested on exact version, scan hash, SBOM) | Numbers come from real runs |

Plan: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/MASTER-PLAN.md` sections 4.1-4.3, 4.10 and R0; code audit `G-gaps.md`. **Nothing here is wired into the build pipeline yet** (`lib/modbuilder/create.ts` is unchanged): builds still run exactly as before, and the new tables stay empty until a later slice writes to them.

**Version-support registry** (`lib/cyrus/versions/registry.{ts,json}`, R0 day 1). One row per Minecraft version: family, `javaRelease` (21 for 1.21.x, 25 for 26.x), `status` (supported / preview / legacy / blocked), `buildable` (true only for what the build service compiles today: 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11), exact `paperCoordinate` (null for 26.x until a stable build is pinned), resource/data pack formats (null = unverified, consumers fail closed) and capability flags (`itemModelDefinitions` 1.21.4+, `dialogApi` 1.21.7+, `adventure5`). `resourcePackFormat()` replaces the old `packFormatFor` guesswork. The same JSON is readable by the plain-Node build service.

**Layout.** `lib/cyrus/engine-core/` is the game-agnostic core and must never name a game; `lib/cyrus/adapters/` holds the per-game facts.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `engine-core/spec.ts` | ModSpec v1 (Zod) + `validateModSpec` + `migrateSpec` + `modSpecJsonSchema()` |
| `engine-core/modspec.v1.schema.json` | the portable JSON Schema contract; regenerate with `npx tsx scripts/cyrus-modspec-schema.ts` (a test fails while it is stale) |
| `engine-core/identifiers.ts` | namespaces, identifier formats, glyph codepoints, `detectCollisions` (pure) |
| `engine-core/revisions.ts` | manifest validation, `diffManifests`, engine record (pure) |
| `engine-core/store.ts` | the only writer of the four tables (server only) |
| `engine-core/router.ts` | deterministic capability router |
| `engine-core/asset-gate.ts` | plan-tier asset gate + router downgrade |
| `adapters/types.ts`, `adapters/minecraft.ts`, `adapters/index.ts` | `GameAdapter` contract, adapter #1, `getAdapter(game)` |

**ModSpec v1.** `schemaVersion` (1), `game` (adapter id), `target.version` (must be in the adapter's version registry; a preview version is valid but warns `version_not_buildable`; `blocked` is an error), `namespace` (the project's reserved `nx_<8>`), `summary`, `routes` (plugin / resourcePack / dataPack / clientMod), `requirements` with stable ids `REQ-1..` and priority must/should/could, `nonGoals`, `constraints`, `assets` slots `{ id, kind: texture|sound|model|ui, purpose, source, requirementIds }`, `tests` (acceptance plan `T-1..`: compile / scan / boot / functional / manual, `covers` REQ ids), `install` (side, restartRequired, clientSteps, notes). Unknown keys are rejected. Validation never throws: it returns `{ ok, spec | errors, warnings }`, each issue `{ path, code, message }` (codes include `missing_schema_version`, `schema_too_new`, `no_migration`, `unknown_game`, `unknown_version`, `duplicate_id`, `unknown_requirement`; warnings `untested_requirement`, `route_unsupported`, `asset_kind_undeliverable`). Migrations: `SPEC_MIGRATIONS[n]` rewrites version n to n+1; empty while v1 is the only version. Asset `source`: `generate`, `library`, `upload`, `edit` bring new or changed content (gated); `existing`, `imported` keep what the project holds (never gated).

**Projects and revisions** (`store.ts`). `createProject({ userId, game, title?, rootBuildId? })` reserves a unique namespace (`namespaceFromSeed(projectId)`, retried with a new seed on a clash; `rootBuildId` optionally links a ModBuild chain, unique). `addRevision(projectId, { kind: generated|edited|imported|asset, manifest, spec?, modBuildId?, engine?, status?, message?, expectedHeadId? })` validates the spec (and that its game/namespace are the project's), the manifest (`[{ path, sha256, role }]`, safe relative paths, unique, stored sorted) and the engine record (prompt version, sheets with hashes, rules version, scanner hash, image digest, model, toolchain: only what is known), then appends under a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the project row: gap-free `seq`, `parentId` = previous head, head moves; `expectedHeadId` gives an optimistic `stale_head` refusal. `setRevisionStatus` is the one allowed change: pending -> passed | failed, once; a pass becomes `lastPassingRevisionId` only if it is newer than the current one, so a later failure never loses the last good revision. `getHead`, `lastPassing`, `listRevisions`, `diffRevisions` (added / removed / changed files), `revertTo(projectId, targetId)` = a NEW `revert` revision copying the target's spec, manifest, build link and status (`revertOfId`, `engine.revertOf`); history is kept. `recordAsset` stores content-addressed assets (same content twice = one row). Errors are `EngineStoreError` with a `code`.

**Immutability in the database.** Section 2 of the manual migration adds a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger on `CyrusRevision`: any change to content columns raises, and `status` may only go pending -> passed | failed. `prisma db push` does not create triggers, so it is applied by hand with the migration (the DB test applies the same SQL to its throwaway DB). Deletes stay allowed (account/project deletion).

**Namespaces and identifiers.** Kinds `item`, `model` (path with `/`), `sound` (dotted), `permission` and `config` (`nx_x.a.b`), `command`, `recipe`, `glyph`; `buildIdentifier(ns, kind, key)`, `parseIdentifier`, `validateIdentifier(kind, id, ownNamespace)`. `CyrusIdentifier` is unique per (namespace, kind, key); `reserveIdentifier` is idempotent. Glyphs: each namespace has a home block of 256 codepoints in the supplementary Private Use Areas (U+F0000 and U+100000 planes, 510 blocks; the crowded BMP PUA is not used); a full block moves on to the next. `codepoint` is unique across ALL projects, so Mod Packs cannot collide on glyphs. `detectCollisions(records)` (pure) reports duplicate ids (case-insensitive), duplicate codepoints and invalid ids across any set: a project, a pack, a server.

**GameAdapter** (`adapters/types.ts`, MASTER-PLAN 4.10): artifact types per route with availability `available | planned | unsupported`, default route, toolchain profile (compiler, release per version, scanner path), knowledge source, version list with capabilities, asset delivery per kind, install rules, test lane, maturity (`planned | template | beta | stable`) and the router's `routeRules`. **Minecraft** (`adapters/minecraft.ts`) reads the version registry and `lib/cyrus/games/minecraft.ts` and changes neither; maturity `beta`; only `plugin` is available today; `resourcePack` and `dataPack` are `planned`; `clientMod` is `unsupported`; all four asset kinds deliver via a server-pushed resource pack (planned); boot/functional tests `planned`.

**Capability router** (`router.ts`, no AI call). `routeSpec(spec, adapter, { prompt?, gate?: { plan } })` matches the adapter's rules against summary + requirements + asset purposes + prompt (never non-goals or constraints) and asset kinds, and returns `routes`, split into `available / planned / unsupported`, a `label` (`plugin`, `plugin+resourcePack`, `dataPack`, ... or `clientMod-unsupported`), `buildableNow`, `limits` (`info | warn | block` with plain-English text) and the matched rule ids. Minecraft limits: custom blocks, free-form HUD widgets, keybinds and custom sky need a client mod; native entity models need a client mod (skinned vanilla mobs / display entities instead); Dialog API needs 1.21.7+; item models need 1.21.4+; worldgen needs a restart; a preview or unknown target version blocks; planned routes say "not built yet". With `gate`, the asset gate runs first and strips gated assets (warn limits `asset_gate:<id>`), and a gated asset named only in words adds a `<rule>:plan` notice instead of a route.

**Plan-tier asset gate** (`asset-gate.ts`, owner decisions). `canAsset(plan, kind, op)`: `create` and `edit` (also automatic generation inside a build, library picks and uploads) need `saka` for sound and `all` for texture; `model` and `ui` follow texture (top plan). `keep`, `install`, `export`, `rebuild`, `import` (your own mod) and `compose` (Mod Packs) are never gated, for any plan or none. Unknown plan / token state -> `plan_unknown` denial for create/edit only (fail closed). `normalizePlan` is the one mapping of plan names (`all` = `yakko` = "All models"; free, katara, saka). `gateSpecAssets` lists denials (the build service request must run it again), `downgradeSpecAssets` strips gated slots with a customer-visible reason and leaves requirements in place. Wiring into `gateBuild`/`create.ts` is left for the asset slice (R1): builds carry no spec or assets yet, so there is nothing to gate there today.

**Tests.** `test/cyrus-engine-core.test.ts` (pure: spec, migrations, JSON Schema file, identifiers, collisions, manifests, adapter, router, the 40-case gate matrix and more). `test/cyrus-engine-store-db.test.ts` (opt-in, throwaway DB only): `devhost db push`, then `devhost run --lock -- env CYRUS_ENGINE_DB_TEST=1 npx tsx --test test/cyrus-engine-store-db.test.ts`.

**Deploy (owner).** Review and apply `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-10-cyrus-engine-core.sql` (four new tables + the trigger; no ALTER/DROP of anything existing). Nothing in the app reads the tables yet, so the migration can land before or with the code.

## Cyrus Test Flight (R0)

"Test Flight lite" (2026-10-10, branch `feature/cyrus-r0`, **not wired into the build path, nothing deployed**): boot ONE throwaway real Paper server for one registry version on node-2, load the given plugin jars / datapacks, run the checks, tear it down, return a JSON report. Master plan 4.6.

**Files**
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/runner.js`: the runner (plain Node, no deps; runs on node-2 as root). `node runner.js run <resolved-spec.json>` prints the report JSON; `node runner.js setup 21|25` fetches + verifies a pinned JDK.
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/lib.js`: its pure helpers (log matchers + default ignores, plugin.yml-from-jar reader, `plugins` reply parser, RCON wire format, server.properties, resolved-spec validation).
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/fixtures/`: `hello` (positive control, `/tfhello`), `broken` (throws in onEnable), `datapack-tf_smoke` (one function), `build.sh` (javac `--release N -proc:none` against a classpath file + reproducible `jar --date`, same as the build service).
- `lib/cyrus/testflight/types.ts` (spec/report types), `spec.ts` (`validateSpec`, `resolveSpec`, `requiredStages`; fail closed on the registry), `summary.ts` (`summarize`, `mergeSummaries`, `describe`), `client.ts` (`runTestFlight`, `sshRemote`, injectable `Remote`).
- Spec extras (added with pack delivery): `files` (small text files placed under `plugins/` before boot, max 16 x 64 KB) and per-RCON-check `writeFile` / `waitMs` (replace a file, optionally wait up to 30 s, then send the command), so a plugin's config reload can be tested. Both validators (`spec.ts`, `lib.js`) confine paths to `plugins/<plain segments>`.
- Tests: `test/cyrus-testflight.test.ts` (pure, 24 tests), `test/cyrus-testflight-real.ts` (real node-2 runs, run by hand: `tsx test/cyrus-testflight-real.ts all --out r.json`).
- Registry: `paperBuild`/`paperServerSha256` now also pin the **server** jar for 1.21.11 (build 132, Fill STABLE). A version without a server pin cannot be test-flown (1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8 and 26.3 today).

**Checks, in order** (each `pass` / `fail` / `not_run` with evidence lines; a check never passes unless it ran):
1. `boot_done`: a `Done (Xs)!` line within `bootSec` (default 180).
2. `plugins_enabled`: per plugin (name read from the jar's plugin.yml / paper-plugin.yml): log has `Enabling <name> v`, no `Error occurred while enabling`, no `Disabling <name>` before stop, and the RCON `plugins` listing shows it green (red = disabled = fail).
3. `startup_log_clean`: default matchers (ERROR/FATAL level, exception headers, enable/load errors, datapack load errors) over the log up to the Done line. Spec `logMatchers` replace them (an empty list is refused), `logIgnore` adds ignores. The two built-in ignores cover only noise the sandbox itself causes (no internet: Mojang public-key fetch, Paper version fetch); ignored lines are counted in the evidence.
4. `rcon_checks`: spec commands with `expect`/`expectNot` substrings (colour codes stripped), plus an automatic `datapack list enabled` check per datapack. stop/restart/op/deop/reload are reserved.
5. `clean_stop`: `stop` over RCON (stdin fallback), exit code 0 within `stopSec`, no matcher hits during shutdown.
6. `no_leaks`: our java PID gone, no process anywhere carrying this run's `-Dnxeon.testflight.run=<runId>` marker, no listening port in the reserved range (checked inside the netns and on the host).

**Verdict** (`summary.ts`, pure): required stages come from the spec we sent (boot, log, stop, leaks always; plugins if any plugin; rcon if any command or datapack; plus `requireStages`), not from the runner's flags. Any required fail = `failed`; any required stage missing / `not_run` / "pass" with no evidence = `incomplete`; `busy` and `error` reports are never success. `success` is true only for `passed`.

**Safety on node-2** (shared build host): one flight at a time (`flock -n` on `TF_ROOT/testflight.lock`; a second caller gets `status: "busy"` immediately, exit 75); the server runs in a private network namespace (`unshare --net`, loopback only: no internet, cannot reach or collide with host ports) as uid/gid 65534 with `no_new_privs`, `nice 10`, `-Xmx1g` max, SerialGC, 2 visible CPUs, an RSS watchdog (default 1800 MB) and a hard timeout (runner `totalSec` default 420 + an outer `timeout -s KILL`); kills are only ever by exact PID after re-checking the marker in `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`; the run dir and the upload inbox are always removed. Paper jars are fetched from the Fill API only when Fill's sha256 equals the registry pin, then pre-patched once (`paperclip.patchonly`, `bundlerRepoDir`) into a root-owned cache the server cannot write. Plugin jars are re-hashed on node-2 against the hash the invoker computed.

**node-2 layout** (`TF_ROOT=/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/testflight`, about 1.5 GB): `jdk/21` (Temurin 21.0.12.1+1, sha256 ce79869e...bcfaee94) and `jdk/25` (Temurin 25.0.4.1+1, sha256 dbb69839...215cf41e), both checked against the Adoptium API; `dl/` (tarballs by sha256); `paper/<sha256>/` (server jar + pre-patched libraries); `runner/` (the invoker pushes `runner.js`/`lib.js` whenever their hash differs from the repo); `runs/` (per-flight dirs, removed); `inbox/` (uploads, removed; `inbox/fx` holds the fixture jars); `reports/<runId>.json`; `classpath/1.21.11.txt` (+ `.sha256`) and `gradle-home/` from resolving the 1.21.11 compile classpath with the template (Gradle 8.14.3 on JDK 21, 24.7 s, 850 MB peak).

**Measured on node-2 (2026-10-10, RAN)**, Done-line wall time from JVM spawn and peak RSS (VmHWM), tiny flat world, `-Xmx1g`:

| Version | JDK | Plugin | Boot (wall) | Paper "Done" | Peak RSS | Whole flight (runner) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 26.2 b133 | 25 | HelloR0 + datapack | 10.6 s | 9.2 s | 803 MB | 13.5 s |
| 26.2 b133 | 25 | TfBroken | 10.6 s | 9.3 s | 762 MB | 12.4 s |
| 26.1.2 b74 | 25 | none | 10.4-10.8 s | 9.3-9.4 s | 722-729 MB | 12.2-16.8 s |
| 1.21.11 b132 | 21 | TfHello + datapack | 18.0 s | 16.6 s | 878 MB | 20.4 s |

One-off per Paper jar: download + pre-patch about 5 s. End to end from the primary over ssh adds about 5-10 s (each ssh connection to node-2 costs about 2.2 s; the invoker uses two: runner hash check, then one call that uploads a tar of artifacts + spec and runs the flight). The research estimate (20-45 s boot, 1.0-1.5 GB) was pessimistic: plan for about 20 s and 1 GB per flight. Capacity: one flight at a time by design, so about 3 flights a minute on 26.x and 2 on 1.21.11, using about 1 GB RAM and up to 2 cores while it runs.

**Results of the real runs (RAN)**: HelloR0 on 26.2 passed all 6 checks (`/hellor0` answered, `function tf:hello` ran, `file/tf_smoke` enabled); TfBroken on 26.2 failed `plugins_enabled` and `startup_log_clean` with the enable-error line, the `IllegalStateException` header and the red `plugins` entry as evidence (boot/stop/leaks still pass); TfHello compiled with JDK 21 `--release 21` against the template-resolved 1.21.11 classpath passed all 6 on Paper 1.21.11; a second flight started 4 s into another came back `busy` with every check `not_run` while the first passed. After the runs: no process with the marker, no port in 47100-47199, empty `runs/` and inbox (verified). An earlier 1.21.11 run correctly FAILED its log check because `-Dcom.mojang.eula.agree` logs at ERROR level on 1.21.11; the flag was removed (eula.txt is written instead).

**NOT RUN / not covered**: no player or bot joins (PlayerJoin listeners, GUIs, the resource-pack prompt are untested; `resourcePack` is only written to server.properties and reported `exercised: false`); no MockBukkit or Mineflayer scenarios; Paper 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8 and 26.3 have no server pin; the runner runs as root on node-2 and only the server drops privileges (no container/cgroup limits; a cgroup memory cap via systemd-run would be the next hardening step).

**Hand-off: how the portal/worker would call it** (not wired yet): from a worker job (never a request handler; a flight takes 15-30 s), after a successful build: `const { summary, report } = await runTestFlight({ version, plugins: [{ localPath: jarPath, sha256 }], datapacks, rcon: [{ command: "plugins", expect: [pluginName] }, ...specChecks] })`. Store `report` (it carries the runner hash, JDK + Paper sha256s, artifact sha256s) next to the build's engine-release record, and show `describe(summary)`; only `summary.success` may show a "booted on Paper X" badge. On `busy`, requeue with backoff (do not run in parallel). Run it from the primary (the worker host) via `sshRemote()`; the build VM 88001 is not involved. For a version matrix, run sequentially and combine with `mergeSummaries`.

**Owner actions**: none to deploy. Decide later (a) whether to gate publishing on `summary.success` once wired, (b) whether to pin Paper server builds for 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8 so they can be test-flown, (c) whether to add cgroup limits (systemd-run scope) on node-2 for the flight. Cleanup when no longer needed: `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/testflight` (about 1.5 GB) and `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/r0-26x` (about 2 GB, the 26.x lane probe, still used as the source of the HelloR0 fixture jar and the 26.2 classpath).

## Cyrus pack delivery (R0)

## Cyrus asset slice (R1)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r1` (from `feature/cyrus-r0`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 4.2-4.7 and R1 day 5 (textures); GAPS findings 5, 10, 15 and section D (Style DNA, quality bar). **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** No real model build ran: the build service was exercised only through the fake-CLI pipeline test. Sounds are designed to plug into the same path next (see "Sound slice interface").

**The flow.** Build request -> server-side plan gate -> the build service's AI writes texture SPEC files (the existing DSL, Read/Write/Edit only) -> the service validates/renders/quality-checks them like code (bounded repairs) and returns them with the jar -> the portal re-validates, renders the deterministic pack through the version registry, hosts it, computes the Pack Loader entry and records a revision -> (flag-gated) the worker installs the Pack Loader and writes `packs.json` after the jar install.

### 1. Build request (`lib/modbuilder/create.ts`, `lib/cyrus/assets/{kinds,plan,request}.ts`)
- What is REQUESTED: `body.assets` (`["texture"]` or `{ texture: true }`, a request only, never a permission), asset words the Minecraft adapter's route rules recognise in the prompt / change request (`item_model` -> texture, `custom_sound` -> sound), and kinds the base build already has (a change keeps working on them). Passed through `POST /api/mod-builder/builds` and `POST /api/cyrus/generate`.
- What is ALLOWED (`planBuildAssets`, pure): the R0 gate `canAsset(plan, kind, create|edit)` with the plan from the real lookup `tierOf(userId)` (CyrusPlan + admin override; a lookup error = unknown = fail closed), then the version (`itemModelDefinitions`, 1.21.4+; 1.21.1 is refused with "Custom textures need Minecraft 1.21.4 or newer ... Pick 1.21.4 or newer"), then `ASSET_PIPELINE_READY` (`texture: true, sound: false`). Owner rule: free/Katara no assets, Saka sound only, `all` (= Yakko) sound + texture. Only creating/editing is gated.
- Anything refused is a DOWNGRADE: the plugin is built anyway and one customer-visible notice per kind is stored in `ModBuild.cyrus.assets` (`requested`, `allowed`, `notices`, `projectId`, `namespace`; read by `readCyrusMeta`) and returned as `assetNotices` by the builds API. A change to a mod that has textures, on a plan that cannot edit them, says the textures are kept unchanged.
- For an allowed kind the chain's `CyrusProject` is loaded or created (`rootBuildId` = the chain root), so the build has its reserved `nx_<8>` namespace; a project that cannot be created fails closed (no assets, notice).
- **Byte-identical rule**: nothing requested -> no lookups, no project, no `assets` field; requested but refused -> still no `assets` field. Only an allowed request adds `assets: { texture, sound, namespace }` to the service call.

### 2. Build service (`services/modbuilder/{textures.js,prompts.js,server.js,texture-example.json}`)
- `POST /builds` takes `assets` (`textures.js parseAssetsRequest`): unknown fields, non-boolean flags or a namespace that is not `nx_<8>` are a 400; textures on a version without `itemModelDefinitions` in the service's copy of the registry are switched off (defence in depth; an unreadable registry = no textures anywhere). `/health` lists `features.assets: ["texture"]`. Asset builds are never deduped.
- Prompt: the system prompt gets the `CUSTOM TEXTURES` section only when textures are allowed (otherwise it is byte-identical to before; `PROMPT_VERSION` unchanged, texture builds record `mb-assets-2026-10-10.1`). It covers the DSL (sizes, palette, all ops), Style DNA (transparent background, 3-5 shade ramps lit from the top-left, flat areas, no noise or gradients, one dark outline colour for the whole mod, diagonal tools like vanilla), the checks it will be held to, "original art only", and the reference rule `meta.setItemModel(new NamespacedKey("<namespace>", "<texture name>"))` (no `setCustomModelData`, never send packs from the plugin). The namespace goes in the user turn (`assetsBlock`), so the section caches per version. Example spec: `texture-example.json` (= the golden ruby sword).
- Workspace allow-list: `assets/textures/<name>.json` survive only when textures are allowed. A change build without texture rights KEEPS the base's specs byte for byte (snapshot; edits are reverted, new files removed): keeping is never gated. The model keeps Read/Write/Edit only; `scan.js` is unchanged (specs are data, not code).
- Each round, after `validate()`: `checkWorkspaceTextures` (JS port of `checkSpec` + renderer + quality bar). HARD problems (invalid JSON/spec, file name != `name`, quality fail, more than 24) go back to the model as `repair-asset` feedback; SOFT ones (reserved namespace literal missing from the Java, a texture no string literal references, a foreign `nx_` namespace) once. Bounded by `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS` (default 2) and the overall `MB_MAX_REPAIRS`; afterwards a still-failing spec is DROPPED (file deleted, `assetDowngrades`, a warning and a "Good to know" limitation), never shipped.
- `finish()` adds `assetResult: { namespace, promptVersion, qualityVersion, kept, textures: [{ name, path, sha256 (canonical JSON), spec, quality }], downgraded, warnings }`. Specs are part of the persisted source (`files`, `source.zip`).
- Image: `textures.js` and `texture-example.json` must be in the next image, and the registry mounted at `MB_REGISTRY` or `/opt/mb/app/registry.json` (it already is for the JDK map).

### 3. Quality bar v1 (`lib/cyrus/textures/quality.ts` == `textures.js textureQuality`, version `tq-1`)
Runs on the rendered pixels of every texture (service and portal):

| Check | Pass | Warn | Fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| transparency | only alpha 0/255, coverage 0.10-0.85 | coverage < 0.10 or > 0.85 | any semi-transparent pixel, coverage < 0.04, or every pixel solid |
| palette_size (distinct colours) | <= 32 / 48 / 64 at 16 / 32 / 64 px | above that | > 48 / 96 / 128 |
| contrast (WCAG ratio darkest vs lightest) | >= 2.5 | 1.6-2.5 | < 1.6 |
| noise (grain: neighbour pairs differing by 1-24 RGB) | <= 0.20 | 0.20-0.35 | > 0.35 |
| outline (dark silhouette pixels) | >= 50 % | below (Style DNA hint only) | never |
| vanilla_lookalike | | | `not_run` stub: needs the vanilla texture set on the build host (GAPS 15) |

content.content:
# BUILD HOST — all builds and heavy dev work run on node-2, not the primary

**Since 2026-10-07 (owner decision).** The primary (ns5002569, 51.79.162.96) only serves the live site:
prod web/worker, Postgres, customer VMs. Parallel agent builds there pushed load to 16+, filled swap
and hard-crashed it on 2026-10-06. Everything heavy now runs on **node-2 = nxeon-fsn1
(178.63.94.114)**, inside a capped systemd slice.

Full technical write-up: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` → "Build host (node-2)".

## What runs where

| Work | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| Production / staging release builds (`npm install`, `prisma generate`, `next build`) | node-2, `nxeon-build-prod.slice` | automatically by `scripts/promote-production.sh` / `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` |
| Schema push, pre-cutover smoke (:3095), cutover, restarts, rollback | primary | same scripts, unchanged |
| Agent `tsc`, tests, `next build`, `next dev`, Playwright, throwaway DBs | node-2, `nxeon-build-agents.slice` | `scripts/devhost` (below) |
| Editing files, git commits | primary, in **your own worktree** | as before |

## Caps on node-2 (it also runs ~13 customer VMs — never touch them)

- `nxeon.slice` CPUWeight 20 / IOWeight 10 (VMs in `qemu.slice` win any contention ~5:1)
- `nxeon-build.slice`: **CPUQuota 900 % (9 of 12 threads, raised 2026-10-08), MemoryMax 10 G, MemoryHigh 9.5 G, no swap**
  - `nxeon-build-prod.slice`: release builds — CPUWeight 1000, MemoryLow 6 G, oom_score_adj 500
  - `nxeon-build-agents.slice`: agent work — **MemoryMax 7 G**, oom_score_adj 1000 (dies first)
- every process: nice 10, ionice best-effort 7. Build files live on `tank` (separate SATA SSD);
  VMs are on `rpool` (NVMe), so build IO never hits their disks.
- **Build lock** on node-2: `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock` — one heavy job at a time
  (release builds, `devhost build|test`, `devhost run --lock`). Locked agent jobs are capped at
  25 min by default so a promote (waits max 30 min) is never starved.

## How agents work from now on

1. Make your own worktree on the primary (never work in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`):
   `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main`
   You do NOT need `node_modules` in it (and never symlink one in).
2. Edit with your normal tools. Then, from inside the worktree, run heavy things on node-2:
   ```
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tsc                    # npx tsc --noEmit
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost test [test/x.test.ts]  # tsx --test (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost build                  # next build (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- <cmd...>        # anything else; add --lock if heavy
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost db push                # schema into YOUR throwaway DB
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost dev                    # next dev on node-2 127.0.0.1:<port>
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tunnel <port>          # reach it from the primary (curl/Playwright)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- npx playwright test ...   # or run Playwright ON node-2
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost pull <path> [dest]     # copy screenshots/reports back
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost stop [name|all]        # ALWAYS stop dev servers when done
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost rm                     # when finished: units, DB and node-2 copy gone
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost status                 # node-2 load, slice memory, lock, running units
   ```
   Each command mirrors your worktree's source (git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored; never
   `.git`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `.env*`) to `/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>` on node-2, installs
   deps there when `package-lock.json`/schema changed, and runs the command in the agents slice.
   The node-2 copy is disposable — commit in your primary worktree only.
3. **Throwaway database**: every workspace gets its own `wt_<name>` on node-2's private Postgres
   cluster (`127.0.0.1:5433`, role `nxeon_agent`, never exposed). `DATABASE_URL`, a random
   `AUTH_SECRET`, `APP_URL`, `PORT` are preset. Extra non-secret env: `devhost env set K=V` (it
   refuses any value that is a live prod/staging value). **Agents never need, and must never use,
   production DB credentials.**
4. Only if node-2 is down: say so to the owner. Do not fall back to building on the primary.

## Forbidden (hard rules)

- **No `next build`, full test suites, dev servers, Playwright or JDKs on the primary.** Use devhost.
- **Never run `REASSIGN OWNED`, `DROP OWNED`, `ALTER ... OWNER`, `CREATE/ALTER/DROP ROLE`, or any
  database-ownership command** — on any cluster, including node-2's throwaway one.
- **Never `pkill`/`killall` by pattern** (`next`, `node`, `npm`, ...): it hits prod/staging too.
  Stop by unit (`devhost stop`) or by the PID on your own port.
- **Never `git add -A` / `git add .`** — add only the files you changed.
- Never touch customer VMs (`qm`, `qemu.slice`) on node-2; never raise the slice caps.
- Never copy a production `.env` (or any secret) to node-2. Never print secrets.
- Never build in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`; never `git checkout` there.

## Deploys (owner/root only)

`scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` — unchanged usage;
the build now happens on node-2 automatically. `--build-local` = emergency fallback (old on-box
build) if node-2 is unreachable. Rollback unchanged: `scripts/rollback-release.sh --production`.

## Admin
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh

content.thinking:
I recall that the vanilla bundler jar can run the data generator directly to produce registries.json, commands.json, blocks.json, and items.json, since it extracts its own libraries from an internal META-INF/libraries directory.

I need JDK 21 for 1.21.x and JDK 25 for the 26.x branch, and since Mojang's EULA forbids redistributing output, committing only ids-only lists fits the task's constraints. For versions like 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8, I'd rely on Paper's downloader to fetch the vanilla jar via paperclip's sha256-checked download from piston-data, so running one flight per version naturally populates the cache I need. The patched Paper jar also bundles real vanilla recipe JSONs per version, which would let me diff ingredient and result formats across versions.

For verification work on node-2, I'm planning to run the Mojang data generator with `--reports` for each version to produce registries.json and commands.json, taking care to use the testflight lock politely with `flock -w` so I don't collide with running server flights. Then I'd extract sample vanilla files — recipes (shaped, smelting, stonecutting, smithing), loot tables, advancements, enchantments, and tags — from each patched jar to compare formats across versions.

For vanilla-mcdoc, I'd pin and clone a specific commit with its hash recorded for attribution, but rather than relying purely on mcdoc for field shapes, I realize the data generator's registries.json already gives authoritative per-version IDs for loot functions, conditions, triggers, and recipe serializers. I'll hand-encode the small field-level subset I need and cross-check it against mcdoc with a derivation script rather than committing large derived dumps.

The validator then needs several layers: spec validation via Zod and semantics, id existence checks against per-version registries, emitted JSON field checks against the mcdoc-derived subset, a function safety allowlist, and command root existence checks against commands.json. That's a lot of scope, so I'm sketching the overall module layout under lib/cyrus/datapack/ — a spec.ts with the Zod schema and validation logic, a generated JSON schema file, and a per-version ids directory holding registry data for each Minecraft version.

For the ids data itself, I'm weighing storage approaches since the full item/block/entity lists across six versions would be a few hundred KB — probably fine to just store full lists, but I'm also considering a more compact union format where each registry stores ids with bitmasks indicating which versions they're present in, to reduce duplication across version files.

I also need a function safety validator module, and a data pack emitter with per-version adapters for recipes, loot tables, advancements, tags, text, and mcmeta files, plus a zip packaging step.

A static validator checks emitted packs for JSON correctness and mcdoc-derived schema compliance, while an importer parses existing datapack zips back into spec form for roundtripping. I also need portal sync logic to build and record datapack assets idempotently, and a delivery layer abstracted behind an installer interface.

Then there's integration work: wiring the esbuild entry point for the generated datapack spec, adding a workspace check module similar to the sounds one, updating the prompts with a datapack section, and hooking the server to record datapack assets on recipes. Finally I need to extend the capability router so data-driven requests like recipes, loot tables, advancements, tags, and functions route to the dataPack adapter with honest availability limits, adding specific route rules for each type.

Since functions should be allowlisted and worldgen changes require a restart, I'm thinking about how to gate this feature safely — keeping it off by default behind an explicit flag, and considering whether to compute availability via an environment variable check in the adapter versus passing a feature flag through route options so planned artifacts can be promoted to available when the caller explicitly enables it.

I'll settle on adding a `routesOn` option so planned routes the host explicitly switches on count as available, with the server-side caller supplying this from a flag like `dataPackRoutesOn()` — keeping the adapter as the source of truth while letting hosts opt in.

For "custom recipe" requests, since things like "creepers drop diamonds" would require overriding vanilla loot tables, I'm deciding v1 won't support vanilla overrides at all — only modifications within the datapack's own namespace, plus non-destructive additions like appending to vanilla tags with replace:false (load/tick function tags, item tags, etc).

Tick functions need a safety cap since they run every tick, so I'll limit command count there and flag it as a warning rather than a hard block. Enchantments I'll only document if the per-version format can be verified against real server behavior.

Effects are where formats drift most, so I want to check the vanilla sharpness.json across versions once jars are available before deciding. I should budget time carefully and focus on real verifications: comparing recipe ingredient formats between 1.21.1 and 1.21.4 (plain string vs object), and checking how smelting results changed to item-stack objects around 1.20.5.

Shaped recipe keys also shifted from nested objects to plain strings between 1.21.1 and 1.21.2+, and tag references dropped the `{"tag": ...}` wrapper for a simpler `#namespace:path` syntax. I also need to account for 1.21.5's renaming of `hoverEvent`/`clickEvent` to snake_case equivalents in text components, while simple text objects with color/bold/italic stay consistent, and loot table name/lore setting still uses component-based fields.

Item predicates for advancement criteria also evolved around 1.20.5+ to accept item IDs as strings, lists, or tags rather than nested objects, though for a simple count-based check this stays stable across versions. For pack.mcmeta, I'm noting that 1.21.9+ introduced min_format/max_format arrays replacing the single pack_format number, and 1.21.11's pack format 94.1 would need that array syntax—though I should double check whether pack_format is still required for backward compatibility.

I also need to verify whether function command syntax like tellraw's JSON/SNBT text components and item component selectors changed between 1.21.5 and later versions, but since full static validation of every command variant isn't feasible, I'll focus validation on command roots plus an allowlist and lean on an actual server boot test to catch real incompatibilities.

For mcdoc, I'll check if git and internet access are available on node-2 to pull the pinned commit, then extract struct fields for loot functions/conditions/triggers using targeted regex parsing rather than a full mcdoc parser, capturing field names along with their `#[since]`/`#[until]` version annotations. I'm planning a Python derivation script under scripts/cyrus/ to automate this extraction.

I'm now scoping which enchantment fields and effects to support: description, supported_items, optional primary_items and exclusive_set, weight, costs, slots, and a limited subset of value effects like damage, while skipping newer attribute-modifier formats that changed structure in 1.21.

I'm mapping out which format variants apply per version family — ingredient style, component text, mcmeta pack format vs min/max, entity predicate old vs sub_map, smithing group restrictions, and smelting result shape — deciding that smelting result count>1 should trigger a version error below 26.1 and that I'll skip components support there for now.

For stonecutting, count works across all versions, and 26.3's cookingtime/modifier changes aren't targeted. Enchantment support is fine since it's available from 1.21 onward across all our versions, and I'll add a small compareMc helper for version string comparisons.

I'm also working out the text spec for display fields — plain strings or objects with text/color/bold/italic/underlined — and when they're emitted as JSON strings versus objects depending on version and context (set_name always uses object form per vanilla examples, set_lore uses a list of Text objects). For recipe results I'm defining the shape with item, count, name, and lore, mapping name/lore into components, and deciding to use `minecraft:item_name` rather than `custom_name` so renamed items aren't italicized by default, matching vanilla behavior.

I need to confirm whether lore entries use the same flat JSON-string codec as item_name across 1.20.5–1.21.4, and the best way to verify this is to actually run load tests with lore on real servers — since all six target versions (1.21.11, 26.2, 1.21.4, 1.21.8, plus others) are flyable, I'll run the test across all of them for the strongest proof, each taking about 20 seconds.

I'm now sketching out the loot table schema — type, id, kind (generic/chest/entity/block/fishing/gift/archaeology), pools with rolls, bonus rolls, entries, conditions, and functions, where rolls can be a flat number, a uniform min/max range, or a binomial n/p pair, and entries reference items or other entry types.

Entries need explicit `kind` discriminators for Zod's discriminated unions to work cleanly, distinguishing item entries, tag entries, loot table references, and empty entries. For functions, I'm mapping out the various function types like set_count, set_damage, enchant_randomly, enchant_with_levels, set_name, set_lore (checking the ListOperation mode field names — append/insert/replace_all/replace_section), set_enchantments, explosion_decay, furnace_smelt, and looting_bonus.

Now I'm defining conditions like random_chance, killed_by_player, survives_explosion, match_tool, and weather — deciding to skip the "not" inversion condition to keep things simpler. For random_chance, a plain float works fine across versions even though 1.21+ uses a number provider.

Moving to the advancement schema, I'm structuring it with id, parent references, a display block (icon, title, description, frame type, background texture, toast/chat announcement flags, hidden flag), criteria (1 to 16 named entries), requirements logic, and rewards including experience and loot.

I'm listing out criterion trigger types — impossible, tick, inventory_changed, consume_item, player_killed_entity, recipe_unlocked, recipe_crafted — and now I'm second-guessing the icon's ItemStack format, trying to figure out whether the count field is still required or became optional once the ItemStack codec changed around 1.20.5.

Now I'm working through enchantment effects, validating value effect types like add, multiply, set, and remove_binomial against the registry, plus checking that effect component ids like damage or knockback actually exist for the targeted version before structuring the linear value payload.

I'm catching that `multiply` uses a `factor` field instead of `value` unlike `add` and `set`, so I need to double-check the mcdoc schema to confirm field names per effect type. The enchantment format appears stable across all six versions, with only the primary_items tag differing, so I'm planning to verify this empirically by loading the enchantment onto a book via set_enchantments and inspecting it with a data get entity command.

I should keep the datapack section version-neutral since emitters handle version differences, and include a small example spec for the datapack structure under assets/datapack/.

This spec file follows a DataPackSpec v1 format that Nxeon converts into a real, version-correct data pack — never raw Minecraft JSON written directly. It's meant for things data packs do better than code: recipes, loot tables, advancements, tags, functions, enchantments. A plugin is still always required by the build pipeline, even if minimal, when the request is purely data-driven.

I need to be honest about limits: no worldgen, no overriding vanilla recipes/loot tables (only adding to tags or defining new ones), and no true custom items — just vanilla items with custom names/lore. Enchantments require a server restart, everything else hot-reloads via /reload, and the plugin can trigger data pack functions through console command dispatch or pull loot tables programmatically.

Since DATAPACK_MAX_FILES isn't defined anywhere, I'll just hardcode it as 4 with a comment referencing the datapack spec, avoiding the heavier import, and note a test could verify this matches. I also notice the repair "asset" prompt text seems to have changed across all cases, which I should check.

Actually, that's risky since repair prompts are user-facing and might have existing tests, plus texture-only builds would be affected unnecessarily since the repair function doesn't know the build kind. Better to revert that change and let datapack-specific repair lines stay self-explanatory with their own file paths included.

## Cyrus data pack studio (R2)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r4` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 2b, 4.3, 4.11, R2 days 13-14; research `A2-datapacks.md`. **Nothing is deployed or switched on.** Two flags, both OFF by default (fail closed): `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO=1` (portal: the build request may get the data pack route) and `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL=1` (worker: a built data pack may be placed on a server). Off, every build request is byte-identical to before and no code touches a server. Data packs are **not plan-gated** (owner decision for composition features): no plan lookup happens for them. Host seam: no new Nxeon imports (the delivery uses the existing `MemberPlacer` from `lib/cyrus/modpack/install.ts`), no new tables, no foreign keys; assets go into the existing `CyrusProjectAsset` table with `kind = "datapack"`.

**The flow.** Request -> capability router (data-driven words) -> the build service's AI writes **typed spec files** `assets/datapack/<name>.json` (never raw Minecraft JSON) -> the service validates + emits them with the GENERATED copy of the TypeScript code for the build's exact version, bounded repairs, drop-not-ship -> the portal re-validates and re-emits (the service is not trusted), records a revision + a datapack asset -> (flag) delivery into `<level>/datapacks/` + `minecraft:reload` (or a restart for enchantments).

### 1. Files (`lib/cyrus/datapack/`)
| File | What |
|---|---|
| `spec.ts` | DataPackSpec v1 (Zod) + `validateDataPackSpec(json, { version, namespace })` -> `{ ok, spec, errors, warnings, checks }` (never throws) + `canonicalJson` + `needsRestart` |
| `datapack.v1.schema.json` | the portable contract (JSON Schema), generated (see below; a test fails while stale) |
| `versions.ts` | `dataPackFeatures(version)` (the verified per-version differences, below), `vanillaIds(kind, version)`, `isVanilla`, `missingIdReason` ("needs 1.21.11 or newer" / "was removed after 1.21.8") |
| `data/vanilla-ids.json` | ids ONLY (238 KB): items, blocks, entity types, enchantments, loot tables, advancements, recipes, item/block/entity/enchantment tags, loot function / condition / entry / number types, triggers, recipe serializers, enchantment effect components, mob effects, attributes, command roots, execute sub-commands, gamerules; grouped by a version bitmask. Generated by Mojang's data generator (`--reports --server`) from each pinned vanilla server jar on node-2 (sha256s in the file's `source`). No assets or content |
| `data/mcdoc-subset.json` | field tables derived from **vanilla-mcdoc** (SpyglassMC, MIT, commit `1528808766ccaaac10e64de002b05d3efc31a9a3`, attribution in the file): top-level keys, optional flags and `since`/`until` of every struct the emitters write |
| `mcdoc.ts` | resolves those tables per version (`dispatchFields`, `structFields`, `checkKeys`); outside the subset = null = not judged |
| `functions.ts` | the function SAFETY validator (allowlist, below) |
| `emit/{common,recipe,loot,advancement,enchantment,index}.ts` | per-version emitters; `buildDataPack(spec, ctx)` = validate -> emit -> static file check -> deterministic zip (`lib/cyrus/textures/zip.ts`: sorted entries, fixed timestamps) -> `{ zip, sha1, sha256, files, counts, apply: reload|restart, checks }` |
| `validate.ts` | `validatePackFiles(files, version)`: the static checker for emitted OR raw files (imports) |
| `route.ts` | `decideDataPackRoute` (build request), `routeWithDataPack` (router with the route switched on), `hasDatapacks`, flag `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO` |
| `sync.ts` | `checkReturnedDatapacks` (portal re-validation / re-emission, cross-pack duplicates) |
| `deliver.ts` | `planDataPackDelivery`, `rebuildForDelivery`, `deliverDataPack` (flag `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`) |
| `import.ts` | `importDataPackZip`, `exportImported`, `checkRawResource` (edit/import library) |
| `service-entry.ts` | esbuild entry of the service copy |

Scripts: `scripts/cyrus/build-datapack-artifacts.ts [--check] [--out-dir DIR]` writes `services/modbuilder/datapack-spec.js` (bundled validator + emitter incl. zod and the id data, minified, 650 KB) and the JSON Schema; run it through `devhost run ... --out-dir /tank/nxeon-build/tmp/...` and copy back (devhost's next push deletes files written inside the node-2 copy). `scripts/cyrus/datapack-derive.py ids|mcdoc` re-derives the two data files on node-2 (see 8).

### 2. DataPackSpec v1
`{ schemaVersion: 1, name, description, resources: [1-128] }`; `name` = file name. Every resource lives in the project's reserved namespace (`id` is only the path; engine-core identifiers gained the kind `resource` for `nx_x:a/b/c`, recipes use the existing `recipe` kind). References are full ids: own ones must exist in the spec, vanilla ones must exist in the TARGET version's id lists, any other namespace is refused.
- **recipe**: `shaped` (pattern 1-3 x 1-3, key), `shapeless` (1-9), `smelting` / `blasting` / `smoking` / `campfire_cooking` (experience, cookingTime), `stonecutting`, `smithing_transform`. Ingredient = id, `#tag` or a list of alternatives. Result = vanilla item + count + optional `name` (`minecraft:item_name`) and `lore` (a data pack cannot add items). Not supported: `smithing_trim`, special recipes, `crafting_transmute`.
- **loot_table**: kind generic/chest/entity/block/fishing/gift; pools (rolls = number / uniform / binomial, bonusRolls), entries item / tag (expand) / loot_table / empty with weight, quality; **functions subset**: set_count, set_damage, enchant_randomly, enchant_with_levels, set_name, set_lore, set_enchantments, explosion_decay, furnace_smelt, looting_bonus (= enchanted_count_increase with looting); **conditions subset**: random_chance, killed_by_player, survives_explosion, match_tool (items / tag), weather.
- **advancement**: parent (own or vanilla), display (icon, title, description, frame, background from the five vanilla tabs, toast/chat/hidden), **criteria subset**: impossible, tick, inventory_changed, consume_item, player_killed_entity, recipe_unlocked, recipe_crafted; requirements all|any; rewards experience / loot / recipes / function.
- **tag**: registry item / block / entity_type / function / enchantment; own tags, or additions to an EXISTING vanilla tag (`replace` defaults false; `replace: true` on a vanilla tag is refused); function tags: own, `minecraft:load`, `minecraft:tick`.
- **function**: a list of commands (+ `runOn: load|tick`, merged into the vanilla function tags).
- **enchantment**: description, supportedItems / primaryItems (tag or items), exclusiveSet, weight, maxLevel, min/max cost, anvil cost, slots, value effects (`damage`, `damage_protection`, `knockback`, `armor_effectiveness`, `item_damage`, `mob_experience`, `block_experience`, `repair_with_xp`, `smash_damage_per_fallen_block`; add / multiply / set, linear per level). Supported because the format of this subset was **verified identical on all six versions** (vanilla sharpness/unbreaking compared on every jar, and the custom enchantment loaded and was applied to an item on all six real servers). Enchantments are registry content: `apply = "restart"`.
- Not in v1: worldgen (biomes, structures, dimensions: router warns), predicates / item modifiers as resources, vanilla loot-table or recipe overrides, macros.

### 3. Per-version differences (VERIFIED on the real jars, 2026-10-10)
Method: the vanilla data generator of each pinned server jar dumped the vanilla data pack; the same files were compared across versions, cross-checked with vanilla-mcdoc, then the emitted packs were booted (section 6).

| Difference | Versions | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Ingredients `{"item": id}` / `{"tag": id}` -> strings `"id"` / `"#tag"`; a list of alternatives may hold only item ids | 1.21.1 vs 1.21.2+ | vanilla `stick.json`, `fire_charge.json`, `netherite_sword_smithing.json`; mcdoc |
| Text in item components (`item_name`, `lore`) is a JSON **string** -> a text **object** | <=1.21.4 vs 1.21.5+ | vanilla `voluntary_exile.json` icon `minecraft:item_name` |
| Advancement background `minecraft:textures/gui/advancements/backgrounds/stone.png` -> `minecraft:gui/advancements/backgrounds/stone` | <=1.21.4 vs 1.21.5+ | vanilla `story/root.json` |
| `pack.mcmeta` `pack_format` -> `min_format` / `max_format` `[major, minor]` | <1.21.9 vs 1.21.9+ | mcdoc `pack.mcdoc`; registry formats 48 / 61 / 81 / 94.1 / 101.1 / 107.1 accepted by the real servers |
| Entity predicates `{"type": ...}` -> namespaced sub-predicates `{"minecraft:entity_type": ...}` | <26.2 vs 26.2 | vanilla `adventure/blowback.json`, `entities/zombie.json`; mcdoc `EntityPredicate` |
| Cooking results: single item (no count) -> item stack (count) | <26.1 vs 26.1+ | mcdoc `Smelting`; the validator refuses count > 1 before 26.1 |
| `smithing_transform.group` removed; `category` optional (26.2 vanilla drops it from many recipes) | 26.1+ / 26.2 | mcdoc; vanilla 26.2 recipes |
| Advancement icons: vanilla writes `count: 1` before 26.1, omits it after (both load; we mirror vanilla) | 26.1 | vanilla advancements |
| Loot `loot_table` entries reference by `value` (not `name`); tag entries need `expand` before 26.3 | all | mcdoc |
| Gamerules camelCase -> snake_case (`keepInventory` -> `keep_inventory`) | <=1.21.8 vs 1.21.11+ | `commands.json` of each jar |
| Item tag `#minecraft:enchantable/sword` removed, `#minecraft:enchantable/melee_weapon` added | 1.21.11 | vanilla tags (the validator caught it on the showcase) |
| Commands `rotate` (1.21.4+), `dialog`, `version`, `waypoint`, `test` (1.21.8+), `stopwatch`, `fetchprofile` (1.21.11+), `swing`, `unpublish` (26.x) | per version | `commands.json` |

### 4. Validation (quality-bar style checks: pass / warn / fail / not_run)
Spec checks: `schema`, `namespace`, `vanilla_ids`, `references`, `version_features`, `limits`, `function_safety`. File checks on the emitted (or imported) files: `mcmeta`, `mcdoc_fields` (unknown / missing keys per version), `value_shapes` (the format changes above), `emitted_ids` (recipe types, loot function / condition / entry types, triggers, items), `emitted_functions`, `not_checked` (resources outside the subset: listed, kept, never judged). The same report is stored with every datapack asset.

**Function allowlist** (`functions.ts`; functions run as the server at `function-permission-level`, 2 by default, up to 4 on some hosts). Allowed roots: advancement, attribute, bossbar, clear, clone, damage, data, dialog, effect, enchant, execute, experience/xp, fill, fillbiome, forceload, function, gamemode, gamerule, give, item, kill, list, locate, loot, me, msg/tell/w, particle, place, playsound, random, recipe, return, ride, rotate, say, schedule, scoreboard, setblock, spawnpoint, spectate, spreadplayers, stopsound, stopwatch, summon, swing, tag, team, teammsg/tm, teleport/tp, tellraw, time, title, trigger, waypoint, weather, worldborder; each must also exist in the target version's real command tree. Refused: op, deop, ban, ban-ip, banlist, pardon, pardon-ip, kick, whitelist, stop, save-off/on/all, reload, publish/unpublish, transfer, difficulty, defaultgamemode, setidletimeout, setworldspawn, seed, tick, debug, jfr, perf, test, fetchprofile, datapack, version, every namespaced root (`minecraft:op`, `bukkit:...`, plugin commands such as `lp`), macros (`$` lines, `function ... with`), `run_command` click actions, Command NBT, command / structure / jigsaw blocks, command-block minecarts and debug sticks anywhere, creative mode, `kill @e` without a type/tag/team/name/limit filter (`kill @a` warns), gamerules outside a gameplay list (both name styles). `execute ... run` and `return run` are unwrapped and checked to the end (nesting <= 12). Call graph over function / `execute if function` / function tags: no recursion, depth <= 8, calls only to this pack's own functions. Limits: 64 functions, 256 commands per function, 2048 commands and 256 KB per pack, 2000 chars per line, no line breaks, 64 commands per tick (tick functions and everything they call), 16 schedule commands (>= 1 tick, no `append` from tick functions), 4 `forceload add` (one chunk each). A summon in a tick function warns. Adversarial corpus: `test/fixtures/cyrus-datapack/function-corpus.json` (60 cases).

### 5. Router, build service, portal
- **Router** (`adapters/minecraft.ts`, `engine-core/router.ts`): rules `datapack_recipe`, `datapack_loot`, `datapack_advancement`, `datapack_tag`, `datapack_function`, `datapack_enchantment`, `datapack_content` route to `dataPack` with limits (vanilla items only; function allowlist; enchantments need a restart; client-visible looks still need a resource pack); `worldgen` is now a `warn` ("not built yet; needs a restart"). The adapter keeps `dataPack` as `planned`; `RouteOptions.routesOn` lets the host switch a planned route on (`routeWithDataPack` does it under the flag), so `plugin+dataPack` becomes buildable only where enabled. "Creepers drop diamonds" stays a plugin (vanilla loot overrides are not in v1).
- **Build request** (`lib/cyrus/assets/request.ts`, one line in `lib/modbuilder/create.ts`): with the flag on, matched words, `assets: ["datapack"]` or a base build that has data packs give `service.assets.datapack = true` and a project namespace (no plan lookup); `ModBuild.cyrus.assets.datapack = { route, matched, limits }`; a version without an emitter (26.3) gets a notice and no route. Flag off: nothing decided, nothing recorded.
- **Build service** (`services/modbuilder/{datapacks.js,datapack-spec.js,datapack-example.json,prompts.js,server.js,textures.js}`): `assets.datapack` parsed (non-boolean = 400; switched off with a note where the bundle has no emitter for the version); the `DATA PACK` section is appended to the system prompt only when routed (fixed text, caches per version; the namespace is in the user turn); allow-list `assets/datapack/<name>.json` (max 4); a change build without the route keeps the base's specs byte for byte; every asset round runs `checkWorkspaceDatapacks` (the generated `buildDataPack` for the exact version + cross-file duplicates; HARD problems go back as `repair-asset`, bounded by `MB_MAX_ASSET_REPAIRS`, then the spec is dropped with a customer-visible limitation); `assetResult.datapacks: [{ name, path, sha256, spec, pack: { sha256, bytes, format, counts, apply, emitter }, checks, warnings }]`, `datapackPromptVersion` `mb-datapack-2026-10-10.1`; `/health` lists `datapack`. Data pack builds are never deduped. The service image needs the three new files.
- **Portal sync** (`lib/cyrus/assets/sync.ts` + `datapack/sync.ts`): every returned spec is re-validated and re-emitted for `ModBuild.mcVersion`; failures and cross-pack duplicates are dropped; the same single revision of the build gets `assets/datapack/<name>.json` (role `asset`, spec sha256) and `datapack/<name>-<version>.zip` (role `dataPack`, zip sha256); one `CyrusProjectAsset` per pack (`kind datapack`, mime `application/vnd.nxeon.datapack-spec+json`, provenance = spec, version, format, pack sha256/sha1, counts, apply, checks, `serviceAgreed`); `MbAssets.datapacks`. Idempotent (revision by modBuildId, content-addressed assets). **No hosting**: data packs never go to clients, and the emitter is deterministic, so delivery rebuilds the zip from the stored spec and checks the recorded sha256 (`rebuildForDelivery`); nothing is public.

`{ schemaVersion: 1, name, description, resources: [1-128] }`; `name` = file name. Every resource lives in the project's reserved namespace (`id` is only the path; engine-core identifiers gained the kind `resource` for `nx_x:a/b/c`, recipes use the existing `recipe` kind). - **recipe**: `shaped` (pattern 1-3 x 1-3, key), `shapeless` (1-9), `smelting` / `blasting` / `smoking` / `campfire_cooking` (experience, cookingTime), `stonecutting`, `smithing_transform`. Ingredient = id, `#tag` or a list of alternatives. Result = vanilla item + count + optional `name` (`minecraft:item_name`) and `lore` (a data pack cannot add items). Not supported: `smithing_trim`, special recipes, `crafting_transmute`.
- **loot_table**: kind generic/chest/entity/block/fishing/gift; pools (rolls = number / uniform / binomial, bonusRolls), entries item / tag (expand) / loot_table / empty with weight, quality; **functions subset**: set_count, set_damage, enchant_randomly, enchant_with_levels, set_name, set_lore, set_enchantments, explosion_decay, furnace_smelt, looting_bonus (= enchanted_count_increase with looting); **conditions subset**: random_chance, killed_by_player, survives_explosion, match_tool (items / tag), weather.
- **advancement**: parent (own or vanilla), display (icon, title, description, frame, background from the five vanilla tabs, toast/chat/hidden), **criteria subset**: impossible, tick, inventory_changed, consume_item, player_killed_entity, recipe_unlocked, recipe_crafted; requirements all|any; rewards experience / loot / recipes / function.
- **tag**: registry item / block / entity_type / function / enchantment; own tags, or additions to an EXISTING vanilla tag (`replace` defaults false; `replace: true` on a vanilla tag is refused); function tags: own, `minecraft:load`, `minecraft:tick`.
- **function**: a list of commands (+ `runOn: load|tick`, merged into the vanilla function tags).
- **enchantment**: description, supportedItems / primaryItems (tag or items), exclusiveSet, weight, maxLevel, min/max cost, anvil cost, slots, value effects (`damage`, `damage_protection`, `knockback`, `armor_effectiveness`, `item_damage`, `mob_experience`, `block_experience`, `repair_with_xp`, `smash_damage_per_fallen_block`; add / multiply / set, linear per level). Supported because the format of this subset was **verified identical on all six versions** (vanilla sharpness/unbreaking compared on every jar, and the custom enchantment loaded and was applied to an item on all six real servers). Enchantments are registry content: `apply = "restart"`.
- Not in v1: worldgen (biomes, structures, dimensions: router warns), predicates / item modifiers as resources, vanilla loot-table or recipe overrides, macros.

Everything else stays a RAW resource with its bytes and a reason (enchantments, worldgen, predicates, structures, vanilla overrides, unknown fields or types, pack.png). `exportImported(imp, { spec?, rawEdits? }, { version, retarget? })` writes unchanged converted resources with their ORIGINAL bytes (exact round trip), re-emits edited ones for the version, keeps every raw file (edited ones replaced as text) and returns the file report; `checkRawResource` is the editor's live check.

### 7. Tests and real runs

Whole Cyrus + modbuilder suite 995/995. `tsc` clean.
- RAN on the throwaway DB (`devhost db push`, then `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DB_TEST=1 npx tsx --test test/cyrus-datapack-db.test.ts`): 2/2 (free account gets the route with a real project and no plan row; flag off creates nothing; sync = 1 revision with the dataPack role, 1 datapack asset, idempotent on re-sync and 3 concurrent syncs; the stored asset rebuilds the exact zip).

### 9. Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- One pack per spec file, max 4 per mod; cross-file duplicate resources are refused.

- Data packs are stored as specs, not blobs: the deterministic emitter rebuilds the zip for delivery; no public hosting.
- Recipe result names use `minecraft:item_name` (not italic, vanilla-like), not `custom_name`; `set_name` defaults to `item_name` too.
- Imported third-party namespaces are kept as they are (not renamed into `nx_`); the spec validator's namespace rules apply to Cyrus-made packs.

input.message:
Data pack studio backend is built and committed on `feature/cyrus-r4` (8 commits). Nothing is deployed. Two flags, both off by default: `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO` and `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`. tsc is clean and the Cyrus + modbuilder suite passes 995/995. Docs section: "Cyrus data pack studio (R2)".

**Built** (in `lib/cyrus/datapack/`):
- `spec.ts` with its JSON Schema, `versions.ts`, `functions.ts`, `emit/*`, `validate.ts`, `mcdoc.ts`, `route.ts`, `sync.ts`, `deliver.ts`, `import.ts`.
- Id lists generated from each pinned jar's own data generator, ids only. Field tables from vanilla-mcdoc (MIT, commit 1528808).
- Generated `services/modbuilder/datapack-spec.js`, `datapacks.js` and a DATA PACK prompt section that is added only when the request routes to data packs.
- Hooks in the router, adapter, request, sync, server and textures code. Tests: `test/cyrus-datapack{,-db}.test.ts`, `cyrus-datapack-real.ts`, plus the pipeline test.

**RAN:**
- 92 pure tests, including a 61-case attack corpus for function commands, and checks that the TS and generated JS give the same results and pack bytes.
- 4 new fake-CLI pipeline tests and 2 throwaway-DB tests.
- Real node-2 flights on 1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8, 1.21.11, 26.1.2 and 26.2, all passed, run twice. Log recipe and advancement counts equal vanilla plus ours exactly. Functions, the load/tick tags, loot (the custom enchantment shows on the item), block and entity tags, and a disable/enable reload all worked.
- A raw broken pack: the validator and the real server rejected the same 3 files.

**NOT RUN:** player-side behaviour (crafting, advancement triggers, the enchanting table), `minecraft:reload` picking up a new file on a running server, real model builds, 26.3 (no stable build).

**Verified per-version differences:**
- Ingredients become strings from 1.21.2.
- Text in item components becomes objects, and advancement backgrounds become ids, from 1.21.5.
- `pack.mcmeta` switches to min/max_format from 1.21.9.
- Entity predicates use namespaced keys from 26.2; smelting-type recipes can give a count from 26.1.
- Gamerules are renamed to snake_case in 1.21.11, and the item tag `enchantable/sword` was removed there.

**Allowlist:** about 60 vanilla command roots. `op`, `ban`, `kick`, `stop`, `reload`, `save-*`, `datapack`, `transfer`, `tick`, plugin and namespaced commands, macros, command blocks, click commands, creative mode and unfiltered `kill @e` are refused. Execute chains are checked to the end; no recursion, call depth up to 8, at most 64 commands per tick, 16 schedules, 4 forceloads.

**Enchantments:** supported. The format was identical on all six versions and loaded on the real servers. Adding one needs a server restart.

**Owner decisions:** turning the studio flag on after a paid eval of model-written specs; rebuilding the service image; wiring the delivery job (steps in the docs); whether to allow vanilla loot overrides (out of v1).

**Design calls the plan did not specify:**
- Up to 4 packs per mod.
- Packs are stored as specs and rebuilt when installed; nothing is hosted publicly.
- Recipe names use `item_name`.
- Imported packs keep their own namespaces.
- Gamerules are limited to a gameplay list.
- The service copy bundles zod (650 KB).
